findings.claim: Ferrous and non-ferrous metals can be reliably separated by magnetism.
findings.truth: Iron content defines the families; magnetism does not. Austenitic stainless steel is usually non-magnetic, while nickel is ferromagnetic despite containing no iron.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Stainless steel, Magnetism; Wikipedia, Nickel, magnetic ordering (fetched 2026-09-04).

findings.claim: The answer to ‘Name the three thermoplastics on the specification’ gives only acrylic.
findings.truth: The specification names acrylic, nylon and HIPS as the three thermoplastics.
Conventional thermosets cannot be re-melted or re-shaped after curing. That usually prevents recycling for the same use, but does not make all recycling impossible.

findings.claim: The stated list of ten specification properties splits conductivity into electrical and thermal conductivity, but omits environmental degradation.
findings.truth: The specification lists conductivity and environmental degradation among the ten properties. It does not split conductivity into electrical and thermal conductivity in that list.

findings.claim: Resistance is the inverse of conductivity.
findings.truth: Resistance depends on sample dimensions. Resistivity is calculated from resistance, length and cross-sectional area; conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Electrical resistivity and conductivity, lines 180–199 and 217–220 (fetched 2026-09-04).

findings.claim: The specification lists hardness testing under destructive testing.
findings.truth: The specification requires understanding of destructive and non-destructive testing for physical properties but does not assign hardness testing to either category. Hardness testing may be NDT when its indent has no harmful effect on the component.
findings.evidence: spec 3.2.3, lines 1789–1798; British Institute of NDT, About NDT, lines 568–570 (fetched 2026-09-04).

findings.claim: Kevlar is taught as a composite material in every instance.
findings.truth: The specification lists Kevlar as a composite example, while the manufacturer identifies Kevlar as a synthetic fibre. Either retain the specification’s simplified classification for assessment alignment, or distinguish Kevlar fibre from a Kevlar-reinforced composite throughout the lesson.

findings.claim: The specification term ‘silicon’ is described as an alternative engineering name for silicone.
findings.truth: The specification’s materials list says ‘silicon’, but silicon is an element and silicone is a polymer. Either preserve the lesson’s silicone terminology and explicitly treat the specification wording as an error, or use the literal specification term for assessment alignment.

summary: Four lessons checked. Six verified, surgical corrections are supplied; two specification-versus-technical-terminology conflicts need editorial judgement.
